opportunities.summary: This role is open to suitably qualified PNG National candidates only.
opportunities.description: This role is open to suitably qualified PNG National candidates only. Program Background DT Global is engaged by the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to manage Australia’s investment in strengthening the delivery of law and justice services in Papua New Guinea for a 4-year period to 31 December 2027. APLJ seeks to contribute to PNG’s law and justice sector capacity to provide inclusive, safe, secure and accountable law and justice foundations for peaceful and prosperous communities, equitable economic development and private sector growth. The program aligns with the Government of Papua New Guinea’s (GoPNG) law and justice sector goal of ‘building peaceful and prosperous communities together’. APLJ will focus on three End of Program Outcomes (EOPOs): EOPO 1 – Community Safety and Access to Justice at the Local Level: Communities in target locations, especially women, children, persons with disabilities, vulnerable people and those accused of sorcery, have improved access to selected justice and support services. EOPO 2 – Law and Justice Services Supply: Responsible law and justice sector agencies increasingly provide selected inclusive, responsive, and accountable essential law and justice services in target locations. EOPO 3 – Leadership, Coordination and Accountability: Responsible law and justice mechanisms demonstrate improved sectoral leadership and coordination of national and subnational law and justice services and improved sector integrity systems. APLJ has a strong focus on addressing gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion (GEDSI): this includes continued and strengthened attention to Gender Based Violence1 (GBV) and strengthened opportunities for women in leadership, as well as increased focus on the engagement of persons with a disability and other particularly marginalised populations. The program will continue Australia’s support to law and justice development in up to nine demonstration provinces across Papua New Guinea, including the Autonomous Region of Bougainville (ARoB).   About DT Global Asia Pacific At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.   For more information, please see www.dt-global.com    The Role The Law and Justice Coordinator will support the APLJ’s activities within the PNG law and justice sector to achieve national goals and objectives as they relate to law and justice priorities in PNG.   Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:  https://tinyurl.com/yydkcexz     About You Essential Experience, Skills and Knowledge ·       Qualifications : High school completion certificate or equivalent diploma is essential. Tertiary qualifications are preferred, but not essential. ·       Demonstrated experience and ability to provide project coordination and administrative support with a donor funded program or similar organisation. ·       Demonstrated understanding of procurement processes, and experience in delivering procurement and logistical support, promoting principles of transparency and accountability. ·       Demonstrated experience and skill in the use of computer programs such as Microsoft Office, including Excel, Word and Outlook. Personal Attributes and Competencies ·       Excellent time management, organisational and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities, adapt to changing demands and consistently deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced environment. ·       Strong interpersonal skills and an excellent ability to develop and maintain service-focused stakeholder relationships. ·       Excellent oral and written communication skills and the ability to present messages in a clear, concise manner, including experience in the preparation of professional correspondence, written reports and briefings. ·       Demonstrated ability to work effectively with others, including the capacity to negotiate effective solutions to day-to-day problems. ·       Demonstrated ability to work in a multi-cultural environment and establish harmonious and effective working relationships both within and outside the organisation. ·       Mature and professional approach to work, including the ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines. ·       Demonstrated reliability and trustworthiness when dealing with confidential issues and government counterparts.   Why join Australia – Papua New Guinea Law and Justice Partnership? By joining the APLJ, you will be part of a dynamic and effective team where you can collaborate with leading experts and professionals from diverse backgrounds, access development programs to achieve your career goals, and be challenged to take a global outlook.

opportunities.title: PNG SHI PROGRAM - RFP FOR QUANTITY SURVEYING SERVICES DURING CONSTRUCTION PHASE FOR GWARE REFURBISHMENT AND DARU HOSPITAL STAFF HOUSING
opportunities.summary: Program Overview
opportunities.description: Program Overview The Strategic Health Infrastructure Program is an Australian Government program funded under the Papua New Guinea Australia (PNGAus) Partnership. The program aims to design and deliver high-quality, resilient, and universally accessible health infrastructure projects with a significant focus on gender equality, disability and social inclusion, and adhere to Australia’s safeguarding policies and development effectiveness guidelines. In addition, the program’s infrastructure will incorporate sustainability and resiliency design elements to mitigate climate change forecasts and disaster risk outlooks.  The lack of appropriate health facilities and safe, secure and accessible housing for health staff are significant challenges for PNG, particularly in regional and remote areas where 85 per cent of the population live. The current conditions and locations of healthcare infrastructure can compromise patient safety, reduce the quality of services and discourage health professionals from taking up essential roles. It is essential that health facilities are redeveloped and upgraded to ensure communities can access quality health services delivered by qualified health practitioners. The SHI Program is working to improve health care services in two priority locations. In Lae, Morobe Province, the project will design and refurbish the GWARE building at ANGAU Memorial Provinvial Hospital. In Daru, Western Province, the project will provide safe, secure and accessible accommodation for health workers and Provincial Health Authority staff with new Daru Hospital staff housing.

Program Background Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across the Pacific and Timor-Leste. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of 17 years of Australian Government support for skills and training in the Pacific.   About DT Global Asia Pacific At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact. For more information, please see www.dt-global.com The Role The Safeguards Manager is responsible for leading the implementation, coordination and continuous improvement of safeguarding systems across the Paciﬁc Australia Skills Tonga program. The role provides strategic and technical leadership to ensure safeguarding is effectively integrated into program planning, procurement, partnership management, activity implementation and organisational operations. The position is accountable for ensuring compliance with DFAT safeguarding requirements, DT Global safeguarding policies, procedures and Paciﬁc Australia Skills safeguarding strategy through the delivery of safeguarding risk management, due diligence, incident management, monitoring, compliance and capacity strengthening activities. The Safeguards Manager also supports the development of a strong safeguarding culture by promoting accountability, prevention, respectful behaviours and continuous organisational learning. The Country Lead provides overall leadership, operational oversight and performance management of the position, ensuring safeguarding is integrated into country operations and strategic priorities. The Regional Safeguards Manager provides specialist technical advice, professional supervision and quality assurance to ensure consistent implementation of safeguarding policies, procedures and standards across Pacific Australia Skills. Responsibilities  Strategic Safeguarding Leadership Lead the implementation of the Pacific Australia Skills Safeguarding Strategy and annual country safeguarding workplan, ensuring safeguarding is embedded across all aspects of program delivery in Tonga. Provide strategic and technical advice to the Country Lead and Country Leadership Team on safeguarding risks, compliance obligations, emerging issues and continuous improvement initiatives. Champion a culture of safeguarding, accountability and respectful behaviours by promoting awareness, prevention and shared responsibility across the program. Ensure safeguarding considerations are integrated into program planning, activity design, procurement, partnership development and operational decision-making. Contribute to regional safeguarding priorities and support the consistent application of safeguarding standards across Pacific Australia Skills.   Safeguarding Risk Management and Due Diligence Lead the implementation of safeguarding due diligence processes for implementing partners, contractors, service providers and other stakeholders in accordance with DFAT and DT Global safeguarding requirements and procedures. Conduct Safeguards Risk and Capacity Assessments and develop practical safeguarding plans to strengthen organisational capability and compliance. Review and provide technical quality assurance of Activity Safeguards Risk Assessments, ensuring risks are appropriately identified, mitigated, monitored and documented. Monitor implementation of safeguarding mitigation measures and partner action plans, providing technical support to address identified gaps and strengthen safeguarding systems. Work collaboratively with procurement, partnerships and program teams to ensure safeguarding considerations are appropriately incorporated throughout the partnership lifecycle.  Incident Management and Case Coordination Ensure safeguarding incidents are reported, managed and escalated within required timeframes while maintaining confidentiality and appropriate information management. Coordinate survivor-centred and child-centred responses, including referrals to appropriate support services and monitoring implementation of agreed actions. Provide technical advice and support to managers and staff in responding to safeguarding concerns and implementing appropriate risk mitigation measures.  Capacity Development and Technical Support Coordinate and deliver safeguarding induction, awareness and capacity strengthening initiatives for Pacific Australia Skills staff, implementing partners, government stakeholders, contractors and service providers. Build safeguarding capability through coaching, mentoring and ongoing technical support to Safeguards Focal Points, Safeguards Coordinator and key stakeholders. Support partners to strengthen safeguarding governance, policies, procedures, reporting mechanisms and organisational practices aligned with DFAT safeguarding requirements. Promote continuous learning by identifying emerging safeguarding issues, lessons learned and opportunities to strengthen organisational capability.  Monitoring, Compliance and Quality Assurance Monitor safeguarding implementation through regular field visits, compliance reviews, partner engagement and activity monitoring to assess the effectiveness of safeguarding measures. Track implementation of safeguarding action plans, recommendations and corrective actions, ensuring timely follow-up and continuous improvement. Prepare high-quality safeguarding reports, dashboards, risk analyses, briefing papers and technical updates for the Country Lead, Regional Safeguards Manager and other stakeholders. Monitor compliance with DT Global safeguarding policies, Codes of Conduct, DFAT safeguarding requirements and contractual safeguarding obligations. Contribute to internal audits, assurance processes and organisational reporting to demonstrate safeguarding compliance and program performance.  Stakeholder Engagement and Partnerships Develop and maintain effective working relationships with government agencies, TVET institutions, employers, civil society organisations, implementing partners, contractors and development partners to strengthen safeguarding outcomes. Provide trusted technical advice to internal and external stakeholders on safeguarding policy, risk management and good practice. Represent Pacific Australia Skills in safeguarding-related meetings, working groups, technical forums and partner consultations as delegated by the Country Lead. Foster collaborative partnerships that strengthen safeguarding capability, promote organisational learning and support sustainable safeguarding systems across the program.  Other Responsibilities Contribute to regional safeguarding initiatives, Communities of Practice, cross-country learning and the continuous improvement of safeguarding systems across Pacific Australia Skills. Support the development, review and continuous improvement of safeguarding policies, guidance materials, tools, templates and training resources. Participate in organisational planning, learning and knowledge management activities to strengthen safeguarding practice across the program. Maintain professional knowledge of emerging safeguarding legislation, DFAT policies, international standards and best practice to ensure continuous improvement in safeguarding approaches. Undertake other duties consistent with the responsibilities, classification and level of the position, as reasonably directed by the Lead. This TOR may be revised or updated in the future as required. About You Essential Experience Mandatory requirements: Demonstrated experience working with adult learners, with a background in the skills, vocational, industry training sector and/or experience within a training organisation. Experience working within compliance frameworks, including quality assurance. Strong coordination and administrative skills, including supporting trainers, managing training resources, and maintaining accurate records and documentation. Proficient digital skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), email, and online collaboration tools for preparing training materials and reports. Understanding of and commitment to Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI); Child Protection; Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH); prevention of human trafficking; environmental protection; anti‑corruption; and other DFAT safeguarding policies. DT Global strongly encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including first nations, diverse SOGIESC and people with disabilities. Personal Attributes Strong communication skills and ability to build effective working relationships. Adaptable, with a positive approach to changing priorities. Detail oriented, with a commitment to high-quality work and accuracy. Team-focused, supportive, and able to work collaboratively with others. Desirable Requirements:  Experience working with Australian Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) and familiarity with RTO compliance requirements. Experience working with national or regional training institutions or education agencies. Experience working on aid funded or donor-supported programs. Knowledge of the Solomon Islands education and training system and local cultural context. Relevant qualification and/or degree (advantage but not required). Valid driver’s license and willingness to drive for work-related activities. Additional Information The successful applicant may be allocated duties not specifically mentioned in this document but within the capacity, qualifications and experience normally expected from persons occupying positions at this level. opportunities.description: About the Proposal Call for Australian Registered Training Organisations including First Nations organisations An opportunity to be part of a panel of organisations and consultants providing skills training, strengthening and advice on the Australian Government’s Pacific Australia Skills program in the Pacific, covering the Pacific and Timor-Leste. About Pacific Australia Skills Pacific Australia Skills is working with partners across three main outcome areas: 1. Strengthening skills systems; 2. Training for employment; and 3. Regional and cross-country linkages. The program also has a strong focus on inclusion and accessibility, supporting women, young people, people with disabilities and communities facing barriers to education and employment. Pacific Australia Skills also supports skills systems strengthening and training linked to resilience, sustainability and industries that are adapting to climate change and environmental challenges. In addition, Pacific Australia Skills places locally led development (LLD) at the centre of its approach, supporting Pacific and Timor-Leste partners to lead decision-making, shape priorities, and drive sustainable skills system reform. About the Technical Skills Panel The aim of the Technical Skills Panel (TSP) is to deliver skills, training, systems strengthening and relevant sector expertise from providers operating in Pacific Island countries, Timor-Leste and Australia. The TSP is intended to be a flexible and on-demand mechanism to respond to planned and emerging needs in skills and systems strengthening over the life of the Pacific Australia Skills program. Successful delivery of Pacific Australia Skills requires a broad skill set and experience, which is supported through the TSP. The TSP allows Pacific Australia Skills to support workforce readiness through targeted and responsive vocational training delivered through a network of quality training providers. It is the central delivery mechanism for supporting training for employment through the program. The TSP contributes to skills development and system strengthening through facilitating capability development and enabling regional and cross country-linkages through peer learning and twinning arrangements. Panel Categories The Technical Skills Panel will have five categories of providers: A Pacific and Timor Leste Training Providers B Australian Registered Training Organisations C Australian Registered Training Providers – First Nations D Consultants and Non-Registered Training Providers E Consultants and Non-Registered Training Providers- First Nations This call is for categories: B Australian Registered Training Organisations and/ or C Australian Registered Training Organisations – First Nations Pacific Australia Skills may select up to twenty Australian and First Nations Registered Training Organisations for the TSP in this round, as the TSP is established and training and strengthening needs are confirmed across the region. The total number of organisations selected will be at the discretion of Pacific Australia Skills. Engagement & Remuneration Successful candidates will be placed on the panel managed by DT Global and contracted through a Deed of Standing Offer. Opportunities will be made available to members on an as-needed basis, and panel members will be invited to quote for opportunities (depending on the requirements of the task). Each time a member of the Panel is offered an assignment, a service order will be signed outlining the terms of the assignment. Please note that being on the Panel does not guarantee work. Eligibility Criteria This EOI is open only to organisations who are based in Australia and hold current registration and accreditation for listed skills and qualifications with ASQA, for a minimum of five years, and in good standing. First Nations organisations may be granted special consideration regarding registration timeframes.

opportunities.summary: The Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP), implemented by Abt Associates on behalf of the Australian Government, supports inclusive economic growth and improved livelihoods in Papua New Guinea (PNG) and is helping government and development partners understand and respond to current El Niño-related dry conditions.
opportunities.description: The Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP), implemented by Abt Associates on behalf of the Australian Government, supports inclusive economic growth and improved livelihoods in Papua New Guinea (PNG) and is helping government and development partners understand and respond to current El Niño-related dry conditions.  Existing climate and remote-sensing products (for example, png-elnino.org)   largely describe rainfall or forecast possible impacts. APEP requires observed drought-impact evidence that distinguishes normal seasonal dryness from unusually severe conditions by comparing the current period with equivalent prior periods and an appropriate historical baseline. As many affected locations are remote, costly, and difficult to access, APEP seeks a timely, defensible, value-for-money remote-sensing solution for district-level analysis and, when requested, selected communities or sites. The work will complement—not replace—field assessments and other food and water insecurity information.

opportunities.summary: Program Overview
opportunities.description: Program Overview The Strategic Health Infrastructure (SHI) Program is an Australian Government program funded under the Papua New Guinea Australia (PNGAus) Partnership. The program aims to design and deliver high-quality, resilient, and universally accessible health infrastructure projects with a significant focus on gender equality, disability and social inclusion, and adhere to Australia’s safeguarding policies and development effectiveness guidelines. In addition, the program’s infrastructure will incorporate sustainability and resiliency design elements to mitigate climate change forecasts and disaster risk outlooks.  The lack of appropriate health facilities and safe, secure and accessible housing for health staff are significant challenges for PNG, particularly in regional and remote areas where 85 per cent of the population live. The current conditions and locations of healthcare infrastructure can compromise patient safety, reduce the quality of services and discourage health professionals from taking up essential roles. It is essential that health facilities are redeveloped and upgraded to ensure communities can access quality health services delivered by qualified health practitioners. The SHI Program is working to improve health care services in two priority locations. In Lae, Morobe Province, the project will design and refurbish the GWARE building at ANGAU Memorial Provincial Hospital. In Daru, Western Province, the project will provide safe, secure and accessible accommodation for health workers and Provincial Health Authority staff with new Daru Hospital staff housing.

It will focus on economic recovery and resilience. The Facility supports Cambodia to implement important economic reforms to support the country's economic transition. These efforts aim to encourage more productive and inclusive public and private investment, promoting a resilient, inclusive, and sustainable economy.CAPRED interventions fall under three technical domains including: Agriculture and Agro-processing; Trade, Investment and Enterprise Development and Infrastructure Development; and three Cross-Cutting components comprising: Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), Climate Resilient initiatives, and policy support. GEDSI is at the heart of all that CAPRED does.

opportunities.title: Pre-Tender Notice - Parliament Wing Design Consultant
opportunities.summary: On behalf of the Australian Government, the Economic and Social Infrastructure Program (ESIP) will soon invite tenders from suitably qualified design consultants for the concept design, detailed design and construction phase for the new Parliament Wing at the National Parliament House in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea.
opportunities.description: About the Proposal On behalf of the Australian Government, the Economic and Social Infrastructure Program (ESIP) will soon invite tenders from suitably qualified design consultants for the concept design, detailed design and construction phase for the new Parliament Wing at the National Parliament House in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea. This nationally significant project will support the future expansion of Parliamentary facilities through the development of a modern, functional and culturally appropriate addition to the existing Parliament precinct. The services will be delivered in three stages: 1. Stage 1 Concept Design 2. Stage 2 Detailed Design, Tender Documentation, Early Contractor Involvement (ECI}, and Issued for Construction (IFC) Documentation 3. Stage 3 Construction Phase Services Up to three design consultants will be engaged to undertake concept design development. Following stakeholder review and assessment, one consultant will be selected to progress as Lead Design Consultant for the detailed design and construction support phases. The upcoming tender will be open to organisations that meet the eligibility and capability requirements set out in the procurement documentation, which is expected to be released in the coming weeks.

opportunities.title: Deputy Facility Director
opportunities.summary: KEY INFORMATIONPosition: Deputy Facility Director Reports to: Facility DirectorLocation: Phnom Penh, with some travel to Cambodian provincesDuration: One year, with possibility for extension up to an additional three years based on performance and program requirementsEmployment type: Full timeContractual arrangement: Open to both Cambodian nationals and international applicants PROGRAM BACKGROUNDThe CAPRED Facility is Australia's flagship bilateral economic development program in Cambodia, focusing on economic recovery and resilience. The Facility supports Cambodia in implementing a range of necessary economic interventions and reforms to maintain the country's economic transition. These interventions and reforms are primarily aimed at encouraging more productive and inclusive public and private investment, which promotes a resilient, inclusive and sustainable economy (RISE). CAPRED interventions fall under three technical components including: Agriculture; Trade and Investment and Infrastructure Development; and one Cross-Cutting component comprising: Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI); Climate Resilient initiatives, and policy support.
